claims.claim: Adding q_auto and f_auto shrinks a sample 0.68 MB JPG to about 0.16 MB (~75% smaller), with f_auto causing most browsers to receive AVIF or WebP instead of the original JPG.
claims.raw_snippet: q_auto keeps the visual quality nearly identical despite the significantly smaller file size, while f_auto causes most browsers to receive it as AVIF (or WebP) rather than the original JPG.

claims.claim: WebP achieves 25%-34% smaller file sizes than JPEG at the same SSIM index.
claims.raw_snippet: WebP achieves 25%-34% smaller file sizes compared to JPEG at the same Structural Similarity (SSIM) index, indicating better compression.

claims.claim: Google auto-tagging returns a numerical confidence score per detected category, where 1.0 means 100% confidence; the auto_tagging parameter assigns tags from those categories.
claims.raw_snippet: The confidence score is a numerical value that represents the confidence level of the detected category, where 1.0 means 100% confidence.

claims.claim: Cloudinary requires the upload_large chunked-upload method for any file larger than 100 MB. Per-plan file-size caps are not published in the public docs.
claims.raw_snippet: The upload_large method uploads a large file to the cloud in chunks, and is required for any files that are larger than 100 MB.
claims.verification_note: CORRECTION: the skill previously stated free-plan limits of 10MB image / 100MB video. The 10 MB figure could not be found in any Cloudinary documentation page, and the support article that was cited (support.cloudinary.com/hc/en-us/articles/202520592) returns HTTP 403 behind Cloudflare and cannot be verified. 100 MB is documented only as the chunked-upload threshold, not as a plan cap. SKILL.md and SKILL_HE.md were reworded to point users at their own Console Settings instead of quoting an unverifiable number.

claims.claim: One Cloudinary credit is interchangeable: 1,000 transformations OR 1GB managed storage OR 1GB IMAGE bandwidth, and on PAID PLANS ONLY 2GB video bandwidth. Credits are one shared pool spent across all of these, so 25 free credits is NOT a 25,000-transformation allowance.
claims.raw_snippet: 1 credit = 1,000 transformations image and video processing OR 1GB managed storage for all digital assets OR 1GB image bandwidth high-performance CDN OR PAID PLANS ONLY 2GB video bandwidth boosted 2:1 for video delivery

claims.claim: Setting the invalidate parameter to true on upload invalidates the previous image throughout the CDN; propagation takes seconds to minutes, whereas a version change takes effect immediately.
claims.raw_snippet: you can set the invalidate parameter to true while uploading a new image in order to invalidate the previous image throughout the CDN. It usually takes between a few seconds and a few minutes for the invalidation to fully propagate through the CDN, while the version component takes effect immediately.

claims.claim: Cloudinary's l_text overlay renders Hebrew with the built-in families Heebo, Assistant, Rubik, Frank Ruhl Libre, Suez One and Secular One. David Libre and Noto Sans Hebrew are NOT Cloudinary font families: they return HTTP 400 with x-cld-error 'Unsupported font family', the same response as a fabricated font name, so an unrecognised family fails the whole URL rather than falling back.
claims.raw_snippet: x-cld-error: Unsupported font family David Libre
claims.verified_via: live render against Cloudinary's public demo cloud on 2026-08-26. Heebo, Assistant, Rubik, Frank Ruhl Libre, Suez One and Secular One returned HTTP 200; David Libre and Noto Sans Hebrew returned HTTP 400 with x-cld-error 'Unsupported font family', identical to the negative control 'Totally Fake Font XYZ', which proves the 400 is font resolution and not a transformation-syntax artifact

claims.claim: A Cloudinary signature is the sorted parameter string with the API secret appended and no separator, hashed with SHA-1 (or SHA-256). file, cloud_name, resource_type and api_key are never part of the string to sign. Cloudinary's worked example with secret 'abcd' and timestamp 1315060510 yields a21ad0f63beb4de2e5575204b79ab90bffb02c10, which the bundled script reproduces exactly.
claims.raw_snippet: Note file , cloud_name , resource_type , and api_key are never part of the string to sign, but are always part of the upload call.

claims.claim: The SDK methods use SHA-1 by default and SHA-256 is selected with the signature_algorithm configuration parameter set to sha256.
claims.raw_snippet: The SDK methods use the SHA-1 algorithm by default, but you can use the SHA-256 algorithm instead by setting the signature_algorithm SDK configuration parameter to sha256 .

claims.claim: e_gen_background_replace takes an UNPARENTHESIZED prompt: e_gen_background_replace:prompt_beach returns HTTP 200 while e_gen_background_replace:prompt_(beach) returns HTTP 500 with x-cld-error 'General Error'. The parenthesized form IS correct for e_gen_remove (prompt_(person) returns 200), which is why the two are easy to conflate. Cloudinary's own generative-AI docs use the unparenthesized multi-word form.
claims.raw_snippet: gen_background_replace For images only e_gen_background_replace[:prompt_<prompt>][;seed_<seed>] Replaces the background of an image with an AI-generated background.
claims.verified_via: live requests against Cloudinary's public demo cloud on 2026-08-26: e_gen_background_replace:prompt_(beach) -> 500 General Error; e_gen_background_replace:prompt_beach -> 200; e_gen_background_replace:prompt_modern%20office -> 200; e_gen_remove:prompt_(person) -> 200; the corrected chained example in SKILL.md -> 200

claims.claim: b_gen_fill needs BOTH an unparenthesized prompt AND a padding crop mode in the same component. c_pad,w_1600,h_900,b_gen_fill:prompt_beach returns HTTP 200; the same with prompt_(beach) returns HTTP 500 'General Error'; and b_gen_fill:prompt_beach with no padding crop returns HTTP 400 'gen_fill only available for padding crop modes'.
claims.raw_snippet: gen_background_replace For images only e_gen_background_replace[:prompt_<prompt>][;seed_<seed>] Replaces the background of an image with an AI-generated background.
claims.verified_via: live requests against Cloudinary's public demo cloud on 2026-08-26: c_pad,w_1600,h_900,b_gen_fill:prompt_beach -> 200; c_pad,w_1600,h_900,b_gen_fill:prompt_(beach) -> 500 General Error; b_gen_fill:prompt_beach alone -> 400 'gen_fill only available for padding crop modes'; fabricated negative control e_zzz_fabricated_control:prompt_(x) -> 400 'Invalid effect in transformation'

claims.claim: Every upload parameter except file, cloud_name, api_key, resource_type and the signature itself must be included in the signed string. Signing a subset (for example omitting tags while still POSTing tags) produces an Invalid Signature error.
claims.raw_snippet: Note file , cloud_name , resource_type , and api_key are never part of the string to sign, but are always part of the upload call.

claims.claim: A raw space inside a transformation component makes the URL malformed: curl rejects it locally with exit code 3 and never sends a request, while the %20-encoded form returns HTTP 200. Browsers hide this by encoding silently.
